label: Hero Section
title: Hero Section
summary: Use a Hero Section at the top of a list page: the page’s name, a search field and a filter button, and the list under them.
corePrinciple: Name the page, then help people find what’s on it.

anatomy.title: A title, a search row, a body
anatomy.description: The title sits on top, the search field and the filter button share the row under it, and children fill the body below. The section is white and spans its host.

An Icon Button, ic_filter, Secondary at Emphasis Medium.

configuration.title: The parts, the alignment, the filter
configuration.description: showTitle, showSearch, and showFilter turn the parts on and off, and titleTextAlign centres the title. showSearch removes the whole row, the filter too. The hero gives its filter AppearanceBrand Secondary at Emphasis Medium; Emphasis on the hero makes it solid or bare. filterIcon and filterAccessibilityLabel change what the button is, and filterSlot replaces it with your own Icon Button, which gets the hero’s modes but not Secondary and Medium, so set them on it.

showFilter={false}: the field takes the row.
Change the icon and its label together.

states.title: Empty, or searching
states.description: The section itself has no states. Its search field shows the placeholder when empty, and the query and a clear button when it has text; its focus look comes from Input Search. The hero keeps no text: wire searchValue and onSearchChange, or typing does nothing.
blocks: The placeholder says what the field finds.

sizing.title: Full width, as tall as its parts
sizing.description: The hero fills its host’s width. Top to bottom: 16 px of padding, the 50 px title block, 16 px, the 42 px search row, 16 px, then the body and 16 px more. In a 360 px host it is 360 × 140 without a body; the field takes the width left after the 40 px filter and its 16 px gap. Figma insets the row another 8 px and draws a 44 px field, a 42 px filter, and a 44 px title block.

content.title: The page name and its scope
content.description: Write title as the page’s name, such as Transactions, and subtitle as its scope in a few words, such as Last 30 days. An empty subtitle hides it, but leaving subtitle out shows the word Subtitle. Make searchPlaceholder say what the field finds and filterAccessibilityLabel say what the button filters; screen readers read both. A long title ends with an ellipsis.
specimen: All your transactions across every account

inContext.title: A searchable list
inContext.description: The hero heads the Transactions page. Typing narrows the list in its body, and the filter button opens the filters. The hero only passes the text on; the page does the filtering.

sources.title: Use the public Hero Section contract
sources.description: The guide compares the Figma component with the installed package and its Storybook stories.
blocks: Installed jfs-components is 0.1.78 (23 October build of Biscuit’s main) from the team’s private package repository. Figma’s Hero Section has Title and Search switches and a children slot; the package adds showFilter, titleTextAlign, the search and filter props, and titleSlot, searchSlot, and filterSlot. Figma insets the search row 8 px and draws a 44 px field and a 42 px filter; the package’s row is flush, with a 42 px field and a 40 px filter. Leaving subtitle out shows “Subtitle”, as Storybook’s Without Subtitle story does; a filterSlot doesn’t get the filter’s Secondary Medium and disappears with showSearch={false} (all reported).
